title: Winter North Pacific pressure gave no clear added summer PDO forecast gain in 1981-2025
abstract: We tested whether winter North Pacific pressure improves summer PDO forecasts after winter PDO and Nino 3.4 are known. We used fixed NOAA index tables and 45 chronological tests in 1981-2025. Adding pressure raised mean squared error from 1.104471 to 1.122422, an increase of 1.63%. The conditional 95% five-year block interval for error reduction was -10.86% to +4.08%. Rolling fits, a time trend and prior-autumn PDO also gave no clear gain. The test limits one regional pressure input at a summer lead. It does not establish that atmospheric forcing is absent. Short dependent records, revised indices, simple response forms and conditional uncertainty limit inference. Code, source paths and hashes, aggregate scores, a figure and a separate numerical audit are included. External source records remain outside the package and can be regenerated in scratch.

display.caption: Summer PDO forecast error reduction after adding winter pressure, and aggregate error differences in five-year groups. Lines show conditional 95% five-year block intervals.
